description: A node's own AI stack, as committed config: its own chat surface (Open WebUI) standing on its own model server (infra Ollama) and its own vector store (Qdrant), the declarative slice of adoption item 3 in CLUSTER_INFERENCE_DESIGN.md. Read by peer-node/tests/test_node_ai_stack.py, which fails the build if the committed topology stops being the declared surface the design requires. Cluster fan-out is NOT here: accepting a signed subtask belongs to the task ingress + cluster client (item 5), so nothing in this file can be a vector for delegated inference.
status: live on agx64 2026-11-05; target after fabric Step 88 is agx32 (peer role inversion): Open WebUI v0.13.0, OpenCode engine 2.2.5 sandbox (live 2026-11-06), Qdrant v1.20.0

topology.bind_host: 0.0.0.0:8181 (nginx host netns); Open WebUI is loopback 127.0.0.1:8180
topology.network_mode: host — Open WebUI reaches the loopback OpenCode engine (127.0.0.1:4204), Ollama (127.0.0.1:11434) and the memory gateway (127.0.0.1:4093). Open WebUI binds 127.0.0.1:8180; nginx owns the published 8181 surface and the same-origin /sparknet-console/ path.
topology.model_server: the node's infra Ollama, http://127.0.0.1:11434 (never a remote node's overlay address)
topology.vector_store: the node's own Qdrant server, http://127.0.0.1:6333 (loopback only; declared in docker-compose.qdrant.yml)
topology.why_published: Operator decision (2026-10-10), network choice revised 2026-10-11: the chat surface answers on the node's LAN and overlay addresses. Binding is not the confidentiality control any more — the SPARKNET-FW host firewall restricts 8181/11434 to loopback + LAN + overlay + Docker bridge subnets, while Qdrant stays loopback-only on 6333/6334, so the exposure is a decision with a rule attached, not an omission.

gpu.why: GPU is never required to run, only to change throughput. The committed file declares none; the host deployer adds a device reservation on a node that has one. Docker cannot partition VRAM, so GPU sharing is configured inside the model server, never by slicing containers.

knowledge_bases.vault: the only authored knowledge base; readable only through the grant-checked bridge

open_webui_rag.corpus: structure-only — schema, taxonomy, charters and contracts; never the vault's personal pages
open_webui_rag.why: The operator wants the node's chat surface to know the shape of the fabric without ingesting personal material. The corpus is built from a fixed allow-list and a test asserts no excluded path reaches it, so the vector store never becomes an uncontrolled copy of the vault.
open_webui_rag.embedding: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (CPU). Qwen3-embedding and nomic were evaluated on 2026-11-05; both measured ~20 s per request on agx64 with the text model resident, so the existing MiniLM index was kept and no reindex was forced.

capabilities.why: A node's own prompts are already free and need no capability (COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_DESIGN.md draws the same line: only delegated work is gated). 'cluster-serve' is what a *delegated subtask* would need, and no subtask can reach this stack until item 5; 'sign' belongs to the Master alone and is structurally unobtainable here — the stack mounts no key, no signer socket and no $SPARKNET_STATE_DIR.

webui_surface.declared_not_database_state: Open WebUI's panel is a database click; the surface lives in agent-models.json + this compose env so a redeploy cannot lose it (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 5).
webui_surface.model_filter_env: MODEL_FILTER_ENABLED=true, MODEL_FILTER_LIST=sparknet-chat,sparknet-plan,sparknet-build,qwen3.5-9b-q8:latest,qwen3.8-27b-q4:latest,llama3.2:latest,sparknet-masterspike:latest, DEFAULT_MODELS=sparknet-chat (the engine chat is the default; local models stay selectable as fallback)
webui_surface.rag: enabled, structure-only corpus, backed by the node's own Qdrant server (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 4, vector-store decision 2026-11-01).
webui_surface.proxy: nginx:1.27-alpine host network; injects /sparknet-menu.js and proxies /sparknet-console/ to the read-only console on 127.0.0.1:8099
webui_surface.engine_route: OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:4204/v1 — the loopback Sparknet OpenCode engine. Open WebUI forwards X-Sparknet-User, X-Sparknet-User-Role, X-Sparknet-Chat-Id and X-Sparknet-Model-Id as custom headers.
webui_surface.engine_key: OPENAI_API_KEYS expands a deploy-time engine token ($SPARKNET_OPENCODE_ENGINE_TOKEN); the token is generated at 0600 under the node state dir and is never committed.
webui_surface.per_user_sandbox: The engine starts one OpenCode 2.2.5 container per user from sparknet-opencode-runtime. The container mounts only /srv/sparknet/knowledge/peer-<user_id>; it has an internal Docker network whose only peer is the host model proxy, a read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities and no key/state/ledger mount.
webui_surface.per_user_models: Every approved user gets a private workspace model (peer-<user_id>) based on sparknet-chat, with their personal KB and the shared structure KB attached.
webui_surface.prompts: 16 bilingual prompt templates (EN + DE) installed as public-read slash commands.
webui_surface.tools: Four native user-scoped tools: sparknet_vault (list/search/read/capture), sparknet_memory, sparknet_rfi and sparknet_status. They call the loopback memory gateway with the WebUI service token and the signed-in user id.
webui_surface.bridge_tools: The dispatch bridge remains the grant-checked vault/authority tool surface; it is no longer used as a fake chat model. The static bridge grant tool-server registration was removed.

admin_federation.design: ADMIN_FEDERATION_DESIGN.md (fabric root, fabric PLAN Step 29 phase 1)
admin_federation.signup: ENABLE_SIGNUP=true with DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=pending — a new account lands pending and reaches nothing until the Master (via this node's admin agent) accepts it; self-registration is allowed because approval is the gate
admin_federation.service_account_admin: the node's WebUI admin is a MACHINE account: created headlessly from WEBUI_ADMIN_* deploy-time vars, password generated at deploy under the node state dir at 0600, read by exactly the provisioner and the admin agent — no human logs in as administrator on a peer
admin_federation.admin_agent: services/sparknet-admin-agent.py (stdlib-only): loopback listener ingesting auth-event webhooks (auth.signup/auth.login/auth.logout/auth.password_changed/user.role_updated) into $SPARKNET_STATE_DIR/admin-events/events.jsonl at 0600; --register-webhooks configures the node's own Open WebUI via POST /api/events/webhooks (successful logins only — auth.login fires on success)
admin_federation.audit: AUDIT_LOG_LEVEL=METADATA in the compose — node-local metadata audit trail alongside the event spool
admin_federation.supervise: admin-supervise is adopted into the local vocabulary + bridge /admin/* route (fabric Step 29 phase 2), executed only for requests the Master signed and this node's own registry granted; the route stays inert (capability_missing) otherwise and reaches the node's own WebUI only over loopback with the node's own service-account token

conversation_passing.contract: the /session/:id native verbs on the dispatch bridge (peer PLAN Step 6)
conversation_passing.message: POST /session/:id/message accepts an 'agent' and hands the conversation off with history intact (Step 6 DoD 1)
conversation_passing.fork: POST /session/:id/fork at a message index creates a child session carrying the shared prefix; the original stays whole (Step 6 DoD 2)
conversation_passing.children_and_shares: GET /session/:id/children lists the branch; POST/GET/DELETE /session/:id/share[/:id] declare a session-view/session-handoff share in 'open' status (Step 6 DoD 3)
conversation_passing.native_primitives: only native opencode/OpenAI verbs; no custom passing mechanism (Step 6 note)
conversation_passing.regime_not_here: clocks, expiry, cross-node transfer and the kb-*/full share kinds belong to Step 8 and are deliberately absent

masterspike.artifacts: Modelfile + vllm-system-prompt.md, both generated from the one source by scripts/sparknet-masterspike.py (peer PLAN Step 7 DoD 1/2); `make model-verify` fails on divergence or a moved source (DoD 3)
masterspike.selectable: masterspike is in agent-models.json and MODEL_FILTER_LIST (DoD 4)
masterspike.capability_boundary: the model holds no signing capability — the artifacts are text with no key, no signer socket and no state dir, and authority stays Ed25519 in the Master, never a prompt (DoD 4)

signing_boundary.why_structural: A deny rule governs a process that may later ignore it. This stack is declared without the mounts a key or a socket would need, which makes the boundary structural rather than a permission statement.

network_boundary.host_firewall: SPARKNET-FW (iptables DOCKER-USER + INPUT, ip6tables INPUT) on each node
network_boundary.why: Publishing on 0.0.0.0 also publishes on the node's global IPv6. The firewall keeps the fabric fully functional (overlay, LAN, loopback, docker nets, wg1) while blocking direct public-internet reach to those ports.

not_built_yet: This describes the deployed shape; the assertion of a *live* Open WebUI, a running bridge grant and a working firewall is a target-node check. The assertions in test_node_ai_stack.py are read off these files and the compose file, and are therefore only as strong as the files: they prove the declared topology is coherent, not that a real deployment held. The admin agent is declared here and its code lives in services/sparknet-admin-agent.py; its live signup→pending→approve cycle is a fabric Step 29 `DoD: confirm: user`.

opencode_engine.model_proxy: host model proxy per sandbox network gateway; only /v1/ model paths are allowed
opencode_engine.authority: none — no key, no signer socket, no ledger/registry mount; each sandbox sees only its user vault
opencode_engine.master: the Master admin surface uses the same engine with --single-vault /srv/sparknet/knowledge/master-admin; the master role vault is never mounted
